To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the continuous flow cell sorting of unprocessed whole blood was demonstrated using surface micromachine microfiltration membranes in a microfluidic system.
a microfluidic device has been developed to isolate white blood cells (W BCs) directly from unprocessed whole blood with high purity and throughput.
we have developed a microfluidic cell sorter for continuous flow isolation of WBC from whole blood with concurrent high throughput (1 mL h 1), high recovery (27.4 1.4%), and high purity (93.5 1.1%).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a continuous flow microfluidic device for sorting white blood cells (WBSs) directly from unprocessed whole blood.
the development and characterization of a microfluidic device for continuous-flow sorting of white blood cells from whole blood.
the isolation and characterization of blood cells from human whole blood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microfluidic chip is able to sort WBCs from unprocessed whole blood with high efficiency and throughput.

this study has demonstrated a continuous flow microfluidic WBC cell sorting chip with high throughput and high separation efficiency, and the microfluidic WSC cell sorting chip holds potential as an upstream component in integrated blood on chip systems.
the microfluidic chip presented in this study is a promising tool for blood cell sorting and analysis in the context of integrated blood on achip systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a microfluidic blood sample preparation and sorting chip was developed to isolate and sort white blood cells directly from whole blood.
we developed a microfluidic blood sample processing chip that can efficiently recover white blood cells from unprocessed whole blood with a throughput of 1 ml/h.
the microfluidic WBC isolation and sorting chip can be a powerful tool to facilitate the development of blood on a chip devices for rapid and high-throughput blood sample preparation and processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
surface micromachining is a viable approach to fabricate PDMS-based microfiltration membranes that can enable continuous flow cell sorting of whole blood with high efficiency.
the microfiltration membranes can be readily integrated with microfluidic devices for continuous flow cell sorting and separation applications.

the surface micromachining technique is highly effective for creating microfluidic devices with high porosity and thus can be applied to a wide range of microfluidic applications that require high porosity microfluidic membranes.
